node_notes.jfk: Documented: the Dimona letters (1963), the FARA order to the American Zionist Council under his brother's Justice Department (Nov 1962), and the Fulbright inquiry. On the assassination: the Warren Commission and the House Select Committee did not identify Dimona, the lobby or Israel as a factor, and the standard historians of the nuclear dispute (Avner Cohen, Seymour Hersh) draw no connection. The map records 22 November 1963 as a date, not a tie. See the book, section s11c.
node_notes.max_ball: Irene Gendzier, from Ball's papers, FRUS and Israeli records: the choice in Washington was "not oil versus Israel but rather oil and Israel".
node_notes.nation_assoc: An advocacy group that put the Arab leadership's wartime Axis ties before the UN and the President in 1947-48. The Mufti's collaboration is itself documented (Volume II). No funding link between the Nation Associates and Zionist bodies was found in the sources checked.
node_notes.james_armand: After 1948 the documented Rothschild money in Israel ran through visible institutions: PICA's land passed to the JNF (1957-58); Yad Hanadiv; the Knesset building (£1.25M bequest, 1966). No document found shows Rothschild ownership or control of the Bank of Israel, which is state-owned and created by Knesset law in 1954.

edges.label: US aid 1949-59 totalled $652.9M (CRS table), economic aid and loans only; Washington withheld arms so as not to alienate Arab oil states. First military loan: $0.4M in 1959 (CRS) or 1962 (another study).
Sept 1950: Ben-Gurion convened American Jewish leaders at the King David Hotel; sales launched in the US in spring 1951 at Madison Square Garden.
1951 Independence Issue at 3.5%; first-year sales over $52M; within six years 35% of the development budget (Water Carrier, Dead Sea Works, power, ports).
9 Jan 1952: the Knesset voted 61-50 to negotiate directly with West Germany, amid demonstrations.
Begin led the opposition at mass demonstrations: "blood money" from the "land of the murderers".
Signed in Luxembourg, 10 Sept 1952, by Sharett, Goldmann and Adenauer; in force 21 Mar 1953.
Nahum Goldmann signed for the Claims Conference side.
Chancellor Adenauer signed for West Germany.
West Germany paid in kind, 1953-66.
$845M (JVL) or 3.5bn + 0.45bn marks (NLI); 30% as crude oil bought in Britain, 70% German goods; 12-14% of Israel's imports for a decade.
$100M of the total went to the Claims Conference (one source's figure).
Mar 1951: Eban and David Horowitz handed Acheson a request for a $150M grant-in-aid (immigrants, defence, UNRWA reintegration).
Horowitz of the Finance Ministry joined Eban in the grant request.
About 3 Apr 1951: Senators Douglas and Taft introduced a $150M aid bill, calling Israel "a bulwark" against Communism, "particularly in Iran".
Taft co-sponsored the bill and backed the Douglas amendment of Aug 1951.
House Majority Leader McCormack introduced the companion bill ("a dependable ally").
10 Oct 1951: Truman signed the Mutual Security Act of 1951 ($50M for the UN refugee programme).
First US grant to Israel: $65M (JTA) or about $68.8M authorized (Kenen); FY1953 a further $73M (June 1952).
The Administration proposed $23.5M for Israel, $23.5M for the Arab states and $50M for refugees (24 May 1951).
McGhee declined Jacob Blaustein's request for $75M each.
July 1951: Feinberg visited McGhee "at the Suggestion of the President".
The memo records Feinberg came at the President's suggestion.
Aug 1951: Kenen worked the Senate floor; Israel's share rose from about 1% to 5.2% of the bill.
Kenen reported to Silver: "all this is still an authorization."
Eban suggested Kenen move to Washington (Barda, via Israel Hayom).
1949: member of Israel's first UN delegation; 1947-48 the Jewish Agency's information director at the UN.
Founded the American Zionist Committee for Public Affairs (1951, 1953 or 1954 by different accounts), renamed AIPAC.
24 Aug 1954: the Knesset passed the Bank of Israel Law; the central bank is state-owned (Ministry of Finance).
David Horowitz was the first governor, for 17 years.
Before 1954 the currency was issued by the Anglo-Palestine Bank (Bank Leumi from 1950).
James de Rothschild left £1.25M in his will for the Knesset building (announced July 1957); inaugurated 30 Aug 1966.
Home of the Knesset from 1966.
Robert F. Kennedy was Attorney General 1961-63; the Internal Security Section acted under his authority.
21 Nov 1962: ordered the American Zionist Council to register as agent of a foreign principal. Never enforced to completion; the Council never registered (one 2016 Wikipedia version says otherwise).
Senate record: $5,100,001.02 from the Jewish Agency to the Council, 1955-62 (Barda gives $1.5M; unreconciled).
Fulbright chaired the Senate Foreign Relations Committee inquiry (S. Res. 362 and 26, 1963).
Part 9 of the 13-part inquiry into agents of foreign principals concerned the Jewish Agency; closed sessions, June-Aug 1963.
Gottlieb Hammer testified in closed session, 28 June 1963.
Agency attorney Boukstein rejected Fulbright's premise: the Agency was "a completely independent body".
The American Section of the Jewish Agency.
The American Section was already a FARA registrant in 1963, as agent of the WZO and the Jewish Agency in Jerusalem.
Aug 1963: Neumann, chairman of the American Section, called the result a vindication.
25 Jan 1955: the Council's board decided to launch the newsletter and bought 5,500 copies at 15 cents (Barda, from Council records).
Kenen ran the Near East Report; his affidavit said Council purchases never exceeded 23% and ended in 1962.
Oct 1963: the FBI offered to help enforce the order (Grant F. Smith, IRmep).
13 Dec 1949: secret directive establishing "an institute ... to co-ordinate state intelligence agencies", Shiloah to head it, about IL20,000 for 1950-51.
Isser Harel headed the internal security service (Shin Bet), created 1948.
Military intelligence (Aman) went to the army when the Haganah intelligence service dissolved, 30 June 1948.
From 1954 Angleton ran the CIA's Counterintelligence Staff and controlled the Israel account, "an administrative anomaly" (CIA chief historian); he "saw Israel as a bastion against the Soviet Union".
July 1954: Aman activated Unit 131, Egyptian Jews trained for sabotage, to damage Egypt's relations with the West during the Suez base talks.
Targets included the American information libraries in Cairo and Alexandria (14 July 1954) and British cinemas, with blame meant to fall on Egyptians.
Incendiary devices in Cairo and Alexandria; the cell was caught.
1955: Ben-Gurion launched a secret feasibility initiative and delegated it to Peres.
Autumn 1956: France agreed to supply a reactor; a reprocessing (plutonium separation) plant followed after internal resistance at the CEA.
The battle of the letters, 27 Mar-15 June 1963: Kennedy pressed for regular inspections of Dimona.
19 Aug 1963: Eshkol accepted regular visits in principle, not the twice-yearly interval; Kennedy's 26 Aug reply assumed "basic agreement".
Kennedy demanded inspections; the first visit under the 1963 arrangement came on 18 Jan 1964.
Johnson kept insisting on the visits; inspectors found no weapons programme while suspicions continued.
NUMEC founded 1957 at Apollo, Pennsylvania; Zalman Shapiro a founder and later president.

1965-66: 93.8 kg of government-owned U-235 unexplained. The archive editors call evidence of diversion to Israel "strong but not incontrovertible"; the AEC found no evidence of theft and did not look; CIA records remain redacted.
Winter 1957: Peres and Strauss met secretly; the channel ran without a German embassy in Israel.
Aug 1962: Adenauer approved a secret Israeli wish list of 240M DM, including tanks.
1964: 150 M48 tanks from West Germany "as is", with an option on 82 more.
The US sold $24M of modernization kits on credit and sped replacement tanks to Germany; the deal could be cancelled if it became public.
Oct 1964: Rusk's memo "FY-1965 Help to Israel" to Johnson.
1962: the first American military aid, as loans (the Hawk decision).
Contested: the historian Uri Bar-Joseph argues West Germany was the "major funder" of Dimona through the Negev loan; Peres denied it and Germany has been silent.

The National Security Archive reports a CIA conclusion that 1968 sampling near Dimona found uranium of the same unusual enrichment as NUMEC's missing material; Helms raised it with Johnson (still classified). A 1978 GAO study said a concerted effort could have resolved the question "if they desired to do so".
1948: Max Ball, head of the Interior Department's oil and gas division, met Eliahu Epstein of the Jewish Agency; Gendzier calls it the basis of the "oil connection" (from Ball's papers).
Eliahu Epstein, the Jewish Agency's representative in Washington.
1943: Freda Kirchwey created the Nation Associates, a sponsor-funded nonprofit, when she sold her ownership of The Nation.
Letters to Truman of 10 May and 19 June 1948.
May 1947: Kirchwey gave UN delegates a 75-page dossier from the Mufti's files arguing the Arab Higher Committee was in "active partnership with Rome and Tokyo".
Submissions to the UN in May 1947 and June 1948 (the second on King Farouk's and the Mufti's Nazi ties).
June 1948 memorandum: "The record of collaboration of King Farouk of Egypt with the Nazis and their ally, the Mufti".
